instruction: Go through all my Spotify playlists and remove all the songs from them that are in "~/documents/personal/old_songs.txt" from my file system and put them in a new playlist named "Archived Songs".
notes: Representative instance: the real number of playlists and old songs is unknown at modeling time, so the problem uses two existing playlists (playlist-1, playlist-2) and two songs listed in old_songs.txt (old-song-1 in both playlists, old-song-2 only in playlist-2); scale the song/playlist constants and the in-playlist/listed-in-file facts to the actual data. Song membership and file listing are hidden world state placed in :init; the agent's knowledge of them is gated by (file-read ?f), (playlists-listed) and (playlist-inspected ?p), which are produced by file_system.show_file, spotify.show_playlist_library and spotify.show_playlist respectively. Removing a listed song from an inspected (original, non-created) playlist marks it (to-archive ?s); only such songs may be added to the newly created 'Archived Songs' playlist, mirroring the evaluation (added song set == deleted song set, exactly one playlist created, deletions per original playlist). The task-record entities (songs and playlists) are declared as domain constants so that supervisor-complete-task's precondition can literally restate the ground goal conjunction; all other objects (credentials, tokens, file path, title) live in the problem. The extra trailing ?f parameter on spotify-remove-song-from-playlist is not an API argument; it ties the removal to the file whose contents define which songs are old. The access_token of spotify.show_playlist is optional in the API but is passed so private playlists are visible. Reference plan length is 14 calls for this instance (3 removals, 2 additions, 2 playlist inspections).
